prerequisites: Elasticity and Strength of Materials I and II

learning_outcomes.text: Identify, evaluate, and combine the design actions and loads acting on a construction, applying applicable technical regulations (CTE, Eurocodes, etc.). Model and calculate forces and deformations in industrial structures using manual structural calculation methods.

teaching_methods: Expository class (participatory lecture, conferences, company visits, fair attendance, etc.)
Participatory class (individual or group problem solving, role-playing, application exercises, oral and written presentations, debates, etc.)
Laboratory (activities carried out in spaces with specialized equipment, research sessions on classroom didactics)
Integrated project (completion of a project to solve a problem or undertake a task through planning, design, and execution of a series of activities)
Tutoring (personalized and small group attention, instruction to review and redirect class materials, learning, and work completion; specific student queries; scheduled tutorials)
Group work (individual and group preparation of essays, problem solving, projects, etc., for submission and presentation in practical classes)
Individual work (student study: preparation of readings, exam preparation, exercise completion, class preparation, etc.)
assessment_rules: The final grade is obtained by weighting written tests at 50%, academic work at 45%, and observation at 5%. A passing grade requires a final score of 5 or higher and no written test grade below 4 points. Unapproved parts can be recovered in the first sitting. Specific rules for Artificial Intelligence usage are in place, with non-compliance considered academic fraud leading to a penalty of 0 for the instrument or course failure.
